subject: Segmented uplift + addendum: MSA redlines and Order Form v2
body:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@cloudharbor.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudHarbor Legal <legal@cloudharbor.com>, Diego Alvarez <diego.alvarez@cloudharbor.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: segmented uplift + addendum (initial ask)

Hi Mateo / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the renewal summary. We reviewed the proposed staged uplift in the order form and have two asks before we can proceed to our procurement/legal review:

1) Term: Can we move to a 24-month term with a mid-term price re-evaluation at month 12?
2) Capacity: We want to segment the uplift across three business units (10k -> 25k tokens/day per BU, effective 2027-01-01).

Attached is a lightly annotated order form (CloudHarbor_OrderForm_v2.xlsx) that reflects the segmented seat counts. Legal flagged a couple of MSA items to reconcile with your standard:
- Section 5 (Data retention): need a commitment on deletion timelines for KV cache on private deployments.
- Section 11 (Indemnity/chosen remedies): their counsel wants to add clarity for third-party claims tied to model outputs.

Can you share a redline of the MSA and confirm whether Redwood can commit to the 24-month term + mid-term price review? If needed, we can schedule a short call this week.

Best,
Marta
Marta Ruiz
Head of Cloud Ops, CloudHarbor

---

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@cloudharbor.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: segmented uplift + addendum (initial ask)

Marta — thanks for the clear notes and the annotated order form. High level: we can support a 24-month term with a scheduled pricing review at month 12; we typically document the review as an explicit checkpoint (no automatic price change without mutual agreement).

Quick next steps I propose:
- I will loop in Marissa (legal) to produce a redline of our MSA that addresses CloudHarbor's two flagged items.
- Lauren will validate the order form sequencing and confirm billing/proration for the segmented BU uplift.
- Markus (solutions) will confirm the technical deletion guarantees for KV cache on Private deployments and propose language.

Can you confirm if each BU will be its own billing entity, or if CloudHarbor wants one consolidated invoice with internal chargeback? That determines how we populate the order form and signatory fields.

I'll aim to get a redline back by EOD Tuesday (11/2) so legal/procurement on your side have something to review. If CloudHarbor prefers a joint 30-minute call to walk through redlines, send a couple of times and I'll coordinate.

Thanks — Mateo
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: segmented uplift + addendum (initial ask)

Team — capturing the legal asks and a proposed approach so Mateo has a redline to send: 

1) Term and mid-term review: Redwood okay with a 24-month MSA term. We will add a specific clause in the SOW/order form that defines the pricing review window (month 12) and a non-binding framework for discussion (i.e., metrics to review: usage delta, cost per token, burst capacity needs). Do not include automatic price increases.

2) Data retention / KV cache: Markus to draft a short SLO-style commitment for deletion timelines (we should avoid airtight guarantees for on-prem where customer controls infra). Suggested wording: "Redwood will provide documentation and tools to purge KV cache on request; for Redwood-managed hosted/private control-plane deployments Redwood will complete deletion of customer KV cache within thirty (30) days following a verified deletion request, subject to applicable export controls and backup retention policies."

3) Indemnity for model outputs: counterparty wants clarity. We propose to add a carve-out: Redwood will not indemnify downstream claims solely based on model-generated outputs where the customer controls prompt/data; instead, we will add a mutual allocation of liability that aligns with existing MSA caps and carve-outs for third-party claims where Redwood has materially modified third-party model weights.

4) Signatories / billing entities: if CloudHarbor wants consolidated invoice but separate BU allocations, we can support that via the order form; but we need the legal entity that will sign. Lauren — please confirm how we’ll present the signatory block (one signatory vs. three).

I'll produce a marked MSA (Redwood_MSA_redline_v1.docx) and a short summary cover note. Expect to have that by EOD Tuesday (per Mateo).

—Marissa
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

---

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@cloudharbor.com>
Cc: CloudHarbor Legal <legal@cloudharbor.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: segmented uplift + addendum (initial ask)

Marta — attaching the redline and a quick playbook.

Attachments:
- Redwood_MSA_redline_v1.docx (key changes summarized below)
- CloudHarbor_OrderForm_v2_filled.xlsx (order form with segmented BU rows / billing guidance)

Summary of the redline and asks for your team:
- We accepted the 24-month MSA term; added Section 2.3 (Mid-term Pricing Review) that requires both parties to meet and good-faith negotiate any pricing adjustments at month 12.
- Section 5 updated with the KV cache deletion language Marissa proposed. Note the caveat for on-prem where we defer to the customer's infrastructure controls.
- Indemnity: added clarifying language limiting Redwood's indemnity for claims arising from customer-provided prompts or data; retained the existing caps elsewhere.
- Minor editorial cleanups to SLA definitions to reflect segmented BU capacity (see Order Form).

Can CloudHarbor Legal please confirm:
1) Signatory entity for signature block (legal name and contact).
2) Whether CloudHarbor wants a consolidated invoice or three separate invoices (per BU) — if consolidated, confirm the internal chargeback reference code so we can populate the order form.
3) Any jurisdictional concerns for the mid-term review clause (we proposed California law with arbitration for disputes).

If those are fine, next step is DocuSign routing. I can provisionally route to Diego (billing) and Marta (ops) then to your legal signatory once you confirm.

Thanks,
Mateo
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai> | +1 (415) 555-0192

---

On Tue, 3 Nov 2026 at 17:02:00 -0700, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@cloudharbor.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Mateo. We reviewed the redline and order form offline with procurement.
> A few quick items:
> - Signatory: CloudHarbor, Inc. (legal@cloudharbor.com) — procurement will confirm the contact tomorrow.
> - Invoice: consolidated invoice to CloudHarbor, Inc.; we will provide internal chargeback codes per BU after signature.
> - Jurisdiction: our GC is pushing for New York law on this one. Can Redwood indicate flexibility?
>
> I'll loop in Diego to confirm billing contact. Can we schedule a 20-minute call tomorrow to confirm signatory and jurisdiction so we can proceed to DocuSign?
>
> Marta
> Head of Cloud Ops, CloudHarbor

(End of thread)
